Maintenance Report — MNT-0103-002

Asset: WELL-0103 (NE-07 Well 103, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 03 Feb 2023 08:00 · Finished: 04 Feb 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 18 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0103-0016 on 2023-02-02 Report written: 06 Feb 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0103-0016 at 11:15 on 2023-02-02 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.7% of the pad area, estimated 4.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 328 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 262 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.4 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0103-002 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.52% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0103-003

Asset: WELL-0103 (NE-07 Well 103, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 26 Feb 2023 08:00 · Finished: 28 Feb 2023 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 51 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0103-0019 on 2023-02-23 Report written: 02 Mar 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0103-0019 showed the wellhead at 18.6 °C with the air at 14.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0103-015

Asset: WELL-0103 (NE-07 Well 103, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 02 Aug 2024 08:00 · Finished: 14 Aug 2024 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 293 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0103-0094 on 2024-08-01 Report written: 14 Aug 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0103-0094 showed the wellhead at 39.3 °C with the air at 38.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 10 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

Maintenance Report — MNT-0103-021

Asset: WELL-0103 (NE-07 Well 103, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: rod string Work started: 08 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 27 Aug 2025 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 461 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0103-0146 on 2025-08-07 Report written: 27 Aug 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0103-0146 showed the wellhead at 46.3 °C with the air at 37.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 17 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.
